title: I spent a year and 100,000 lines of coke shipping a Steam game. My take: "It's a myth that anyone can 'one line' a commercially viable game"
author: Rich_Sinq
selftext:
A year ago, I had zero game development experience and a dream. Today, I've shipped my first game on Steam, entirely fueled by cocaine.

Here's what I learned.

**How it started**

I originally wanted to make a simple browser-based 3D maze game. Nothing ambitious. Just a fun weekend project.

Then I did my first line.

72 hours later, I'd built a custom game engine, rewritten the rendering pipeline three times, and purchased six domains.

**The stack and how it changed**

* First \~2,000 lines: Colombian.
* Around 10,000 lines, I switched to Peruvian for better performance.
* At 40,000 lines, I stopped sleeping entirely.
* At 75,000 lines, I invented my own programming language. Unfortunately, nobody, including me, can read it.
* At 100,000 lines, I shipped.

**The one-line myth**

People think you can just do one line and magically create a commercially viable game. That's simply not true.

It takes hundreds of hours, thousands of lines, and an absolutely devastating amount of commitment.

**My advice for aspiring solo devs**

Just start. You don't need to know what you're doing. I certainly didn't.

My game currently has 3 wishlists, 0 sales, and 47,000 particle effects.

I'm incredibly proud of what I've accomplished.

My family has asked me to come home.

Anyway, how are you guys handling burnout?
